I've found Tempest to be pretty effective against the Ennead if you can get his Shackles out and then keep all Ennead members within a couple of hp of each other - that way Squall alone should do three points of damage to each of them. and threads like this is why we started the statistics project.... :)  
Unsafe_Bet, in the OP, wrote:
Since this is all experimental, I welcome feedback based on personal experience (NOT based on parroting the results of the statistics thread, as I don't think the methodology there is rigid enough to produce truly definite answers of what's actually objectively true, rather than what reflects the experiences of the limited pool of people who are contributing to it)  

To be more specific, statistics can only go so far.  If, for example, the statistics thread showed that Tempest won 75% of his games against the Advanced Ennead (we're temporarily ignoring the question of what other heroes he was paired with), it would NOT mean that I could count on having a 3/4 chance of winning an Advanced Ennead game just by playing Tempest.  Maybe all the players who contributed to the thread were using Ameena's method, but I wouldn't know that, would have my aforementioned reluctance to try it, and would be playing him differently than is necessary to get that sweet, sweet win percentage.  The statistics don't tell me that kind of thing - they don't tell me much of ANYTHING, by my standards of somethingness - and thus I don't consider them more than minimally useful.  The numbers don't help me much, if at all; what helps me is knowing WHY something is true, not simply that it is (and of course statistics don't even tell us that, they simply say that something has a certain percentage of confidence in SEEMING to be true, based on the available data - which, to me, is like climbing aboard a bus whose driver has a certain percentage of confidence in SEEMING to know how not to crash into a gasoline tanker).

posts.name: Ameena
posts.cooked:
Bear in mind when I fight the Ennead, H is always three and we only ever do them on Normal. Therefore we often only have to fight thee of them, sometimes four, and once or twice five…I don't know if we've ever gone past seven. It only requires that one card for Tempest to be super-effective and he has more than one copy in his deck plus the potential to get Aquatic Correspondance and speed up the cycling through to get hold of it. We never really have any trouble with the Ennead healing spectacularly - about the best they ever manage is a couple of hp each in a single turn.

As for stuff destruction, Tempest is highly unlikely to be the only hero with stuff in play and I think the stuff-destruction card only takes out H things total, doesn't it? It's not a lot, anyway. And plenty of heroes (including Tempest himself) have ways of getting stuff back out of the trash if they can't outright get hold of and play a second copy of whatever it was they lost. I don't recall ever having any major problem with the Ennead nuking my stuff though - I'd even forgotten that they could…but we don't fight them that often given that we roll for our villains and there are so many of them to choose from now :).

When destroying the Ennead we usually go by "who's got the most annoying incap power?" and leave them till last. So Tefnut, for example, will get left till last every time. If we're doing the "Shackled Tempest AEs everything" tactic, it doesn't tend to matter since they all go down in the same turn anyway >:). The main thing that messes up this tactic if we can get it going is that another member of the Nine comes out just as we're nearly done finishing off everyone else. But that's okay - then we just focus fire on them instead and they go down within a round or two anyway, muahahaha…

Anyway, Osiris is annoying for the forced discard under Ankh cards when active, so we try and take him down early if he's around. Nuit gets priority if she's up, though, naturally…though on thinking about it combining Tempest with Parse (what's that card where all hero damage is irreducible…) would be pretty epic. Or just Parse in general if there is anyone (like Osiris) about who's annoying and needs dealing with through soak granted by Nuit. Though it might be better to just focus on Nuit so she goes down that much quicker.

Oh well, that's the thing about this game - so many options for destroying the bad guys!

posts.name: lynkfox

I don't mean that your ratings are not to be done.

 

I meant that all the people in this thread who are saying 'no, your wrong, so and so villain is easier/harder than that!' 

 

Well thats what the statistics are for. Not to make your difficulty ratings for you. But to say 'well,on average, over a larger number of entries, so and so villain really is easier than such and such villain' At least at a glance.

 

 

Delving into the why is great. Delving into the how is even better. I'm not saying taking the statistics as gosple. Hell, most things on there still have less than 500 entries, so still with (i think, someone did the math not me) greater than 5% error  - which when the range of '% won' 17-40% that 5% can radically change where some character lands.

 

Just saying they are a useful tool when people start spouting opinions on such and such villain being stronger/weaker than others.  By all means, make your own ratings, and have your own reasonings. You can just use the statistcs to help defend your ratings, (not parrot, but defend) and remember there is a large error margin which gives you that leway to play around.

j1hopki1 wrote:


Matriarch: Advanced Matriarch is clearly a 5. The cohorts being indestructible completely changes the game.  You mentioned that doesn't matter if they don't show up, but it's impossible for them to not show up.  
That is certainly not true.  Say she starts the game with 2x Darken the Sky, and the heroes take out the Mask in one turn.  Then she puts out Carrion Fields.  Turn 3 she does another Darken the Sky; by then the heroes might be well-enough set up that they can not only destroy the Mask again before her turn returns, but do enough damage to her that by the time a Cohort does appear, they can just finish her off.  With two Horrid Cacophonies on top of the cards already named, the Cohorts are just 2 out of 9 non-Fowl cards; if you're able to consistently keep her Maskless, you can potentially have six turns before both Cohorts appear, and that's plenty of time to ventilate a squishy 70-HP girl with no defenses whatsoever.  I've had games where she was extremely dangerous, but I've also had games where I just rolled over her, and if I ever really want to make her lose, I'll just play Legacy and that's practically Game Over before it even starts.

To further clarify, I've played eight games against the Matriarch, and three of them were declared Advanced, but in only one of them did it actually matter whether the Cohorts were indestructible or not.  One time, I fought her in Insula Primalis with a five-hero team, and she died in four rounds without ever getting a Cohort into play (Visionary was one of the heroes, so I probably controlled her deck to ensure she played blanks for most of her turns after the first); another time she utterly destroyed me, and the Cohort showed up at the last minute and was basically irrelevant at the time, so I just conceded since I had one hero left with like 2 HP.  The one game in which Advanced status actually mattered was a crushing loss, but I think that had more to do with her +1 damage on Advanced and the fact that a Marsquake killed all the Fowl that we'd been trying to avoid popping while we beat on Lilian herself.  It also didn't help that our first-time Haka player wasted a Ground Pound early in the match when we didn't need it; I figured I should avoid telling him what not to do, as this habit of mine tends to annoy people, but it could well have been what cost us the game in this case.  Regardless, my experiences have taught me that advanced games against Matriarch are only potentially harder than regular ones, and if I cared about what might happen, I'd agree that Omnitron was more than a 1.  But I care about what actually does happen (my avatar notwithstanding), and so far Omnitron has usually been largely inert, and so far Matriarch's Cohorts have been a very small part of her deck.

posts.cooked: I played my eighth Chairman game tonight, and I definitely reconfirmed my opinion on Advanced.  We were three of the most powerful heroes (Legacy, Wraith, and Tempest) plus a specialized weapon for getting through all the reduction (Parse), and we completely destroyed him.  It only took three rounds to mop up all the Underbosses and Thugs, and then Parse stripped the last Prison Break out of his deck and just left him at like four cards while we clobbered him and Operative into mincemeat.  Once the Organization ceases to exist, these two don't actually do anything by themselves, so by not letting the deck reshuffle, we kept them just sitting around waiting for the axe to fall.  It was magnificent.  I now feel about the Chairman the way McBehrer does about the Ennead - a challenging puzzle at first, but easily reduced to formula with a bit of experience.  I don't know how you can beat him with a more run-of-the-mill party, but when the heavy hitters are all involved, he seems to be fairly possible to steamroll, and Advancing him actually helps in that case.  (The only thing we sorta did wrong was kill the Chairman first, since his retaliation damage nearly did in a hero or two; with both Shielding Winds and Superhuman Durability in play, it only just now occurred to me that we should have gotten Oppy to flip so she'd boost his H damage up to 5.  I didn't think of it at the time, and just wanted to kill him fast because he was weaker, so Tempest got the tar beaten out of him rather unnecessarily.)

posts.name: Ameena
posts.cooked: Yeah, he does need to actually take damage. He can be really good against Plague Rat if you can get out the Ablative Coating, the RPS, and an Innervation Ray or two. Then get yourself Infected - at the start of your turn you will have to hit yourself for irreducible toxic damage, against which the plating is no protection. However, that means you've taken damage covered by said plating, so your RPS goes off and you get to hit Rat (or another target, if you prefer, meaning Rat's Locus or an environment target if present). Meanwhile you get any lost hp back from the Innervation Ray(s), which will go off either before or after the Infection depending on the order in which they were played. It means you get to hit Rat for free at the start of every turn, heal it back, and still do other stuff in all your other phases (and that's not even mentioning the effects of your other three Component types if you can get those out as well) :D.
